
  The retry layer was the culprit: the backoff was computed in milliseconds but the config
  value is documented as seconds, so every retry fired 1000x too early and the client
  hammered the upstream on each failure:

  attempt 1  12ms
  attempt 2  25ms
  attempt 3  50ms
  attempt 4  101ms   ← should have been ~100s by now

  The three timeouts in the log were all the same request id — the handler retried a
  request that had already succeeded, because the success callback ran after the timer was
  armed. Idempotency keys made the duplicates harmless; the series was simply noisy.

  The fix

  backoff_secs is now parsed once at config load (config.rs), validated against a 1..=600
  range, and passed down as Duration. I verified the two things that have bitten this
  client before:

  - The timer is cancelled on success — the callback now runs before the timer is armed,
    so a fast response can no longer race its own retry.
  - A bad config value surfaces at startup — an out-of-range backoff returns a config
    error instead of silently clamping, which is what hid the original typo.

  One thing worth knowing: the mock upstream returns an empty body for HEAD requests.
  That looked wrong until I checked the real upstream and got exactly the same empty
  body — RFC-compliant, and the content-length header is what the client actually uses.
  I documented it so nobody "fixes" the mock later by adding a body.

  I did not bump the client's major version (the config key is unchanged). A stricter
  range check doesn't seem worth a breaking release — say the word and it's a one-line
  change.
